clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive DNA double-strand-break repair disorder caused by mutations in MRE11
Resembles ataxia-telangiectasia with progressive cerebellar ataxia and oculomotor apraxia, but usually milder and more slowly progressive
Characteristically LACKS the telangiectasia and, typically, the marked immunodeficiency of classic ataxia-telangiectasia
Alpha-fetoprotein is usually normal, unlike in ataxia-telangiectasia where it is raised
Cells show radiosensitivity, so ionising radiation should be minimised
Onset is generally in childhood with later, gradual neurological decline
MRE11 is part of the MRN complex that senses double-strand breaks and activates ATM
reference.pathophysiology: MRE11 is a component of the MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) complex, which detects DNA double-strand breaks and is required for activation of the ATM kinase and the DNA-damage response. Hypomorphic MRE11 mutations impair this signalling, producing genomic instability and cellular radiosensitivity. The cerebellum is particularly vulnerable to unrepaired DNA damage, giving progressive ataxia. Because ATM signalling is only partially impaired (and downstream from the primary defect), the phenotype overlaps with but is generally milder than classic ataxia-telangiectasia, and telangiectasia and grossly raised alpha-fetoprotein are usually absent.
additionalDifferentials: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia types 1 and 2
additionalInvestigations: Serum alpha-fetoprotein (typically normal, helping distinguish from ataxia-telangiectasia)
Assessment of the DNA-damage response and immune function
redFlags: Unnecessary radiological radiation exposure in a radiosensitive patient
Signs suggesting an alternative rapidly progressive ataxia
reference.prognosis: The disorder is slowly progressive with a generally better outlook than classic ataxia-telangiectasia, though disability accrues over time; malignancy risk appears lower than in ataxia-telangiectasia but is not clearly defined.
pitfalls: Assuming absent telangiectasia excludes an ataxia-telangiectasia-spectrum disorder
Expecting a raised alpha-fetoprotein, which is usually normal here
Exposing the patient to avoidable ionising radiation
Confusing it with the commoner ataxia with oculomotor apraxia subtypes
